chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who buys goods for a deferred period, he said: He is not permitted to sell it with markup (murabahah) except for the same period for which he bought it; and if he sells it with markup without informing the buyer, then the buyer has the right to a similar period of deferment.

key_terms.إِلَى أَجَلٍ: For a deferred period / on credit
key_terms.مُرَابَحَةً: Selling with a known profit margin, often involving deferred payment
key_terms.مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ: Similar to that / of the same duration

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for reselling goods bought on credit with a profit margin in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanics of 'bay' al-murabahah' (selling on credit with a markup) by preventing 'debt chaining,' where a seller extends credit beyond the original term without the buyer's knowledge. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of transparency in financial transactions, ensuring that the buyer is not bound by an extended deferment period they did not explicitly agree to, thereby protecting them from hidden interest-like burdens.
